# ocquota Real provider allowance alongside local, read-only usage statistics, calm themes and a little atmosphere. Cherry blossoms, rain, drifting leaves and seven more ambient scenes live in their own small strip, leaving your code and statistics easy to read. **13 themes · 10 scenes · live pause and speed controls · no telemetry** ## Install or update The npm package requires **Bun 1.4.4+** on your PATH. If needed, install it with `npm install -g bun`, then: ```sh npm install -g @kyzenn.raw/ocquota@latest ocquota --version ocquota themes ocquota preview --theme sakura ``` Or use `bun add -g @kyzenn.raw/ocquota`. The standalone Windows x64 ZIP bundles Bun; extract **all files** together and use `.\ocquota.exe` in PowerShell. Windows 10 1809+ / Windows 11 are supported. Native CI also covers macOS and Linux. ## OpenCode: themes, live stats and ambient motion inside your workspace Requires **OpenCode 2.3.2+**. ```sh ocquota opencode-install --theme sakura --animation sakura --speed 0.75 opencode ``` Restart OpenCode after installing. The clean sidebar follows the selected model/provider. Account allowance appears first, with its source, unit, reset and freshness. Recorded local usage appears separately. No fixed token capacity is invented for ChatGPT Plus or free models. Detailed input/output, reasoning, cache and recorded cost statistics expand with `/ocquota-details`. The footer labels local counts. A local target appears only when explicitly supplied in the plugin options; it is never presented as a provider allowance. Inside OpenCode: | Command | What it does | | --- | --- | | `/ocquota` | Usage and local-budget details | | `/ocquota-details` | Expand/collapse detailed local token and recorded-cost rows | | `/themes` | Switch the workspace to any `ocquota-*` theme | | `/motion` | Pause or resume the ambient strip | | `/motion-next` | Cycle through the ten scenes | | `/motion-faster` | Increase speed, up to 3× | | `/motion-slower` | Decrease speed, down to 0.25× | Live controls apply to the current OpenCode session. To persist your choice, rerun the installer with `--animation` and `--speed`, or edit the plugin options in `opencode.json(c)`: ```json { "plugins": [{ "package": "@kyzenn.raw/ocquota@0.4.0", "options": { "theme": "sakura", "animation": "sakura", "speed": 0.75, "motion": true, "window": "day", "refreshMs": 2000 } }] } ``` The installer copies the plugin locally and installs theme files into `~/.config/opencode/themes`. If `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is set, it uses that directory instead. Preserve the installer's local `package` path when editing its options. The server part captures quota headers and projects account counters over typed RPC; the TUI receives sanitized counters, not credentials. The installer migrates its older TUI-only entry out of `cli.json(c)` so it loads once through `opencode.json(c)`. Theme selection stays in `cli.json(c)`. For themes, run the installer even if you load the plugin directly from npm. Existing settings and plugins are preserved; config backups sit beside both `opencode.json(c)` and `cli.json(c)`. JSONC comments survive in the verbatim backup; the updated file is formatted JSON. Existing global `animations: false` is respected. ## Codex: native themes and footer stats ```sh ocquota codex-install --theme sakura codex ``` Restart Codex. `/theme` selects any of the thirteen `ocquota-*` themes; `/statusline` customizes built-in footer items. Themes color syntax, diffs and the native footer; Codex controls its background and the rest of its UI. New theme presets include model/reasoning mode, context remaining, used tokens, input/output tokens, and five-hour/weekly account limits. Existing footer items are retained. Account limit indicators appear when supplied by the account. Use `/status` for further account/session details. **Codex does not expose an arbitrary animated UI slot.** Falling scenes and the complete local usage dashboard run in a separate terminal pane alongside Codex: ```sh ocquota watch --source codex --theme sakura --animation sakura --speed 0.75 ``` This companion follows live session logs without changing or wrapping Codex. Codex logs do not supply billed dollar cost; reports display `N/A` for cost and reject `--metric cost`. Local budgets are separate from provider account limits. Codex setup respects `--codex-home`, `OCQUOTA_CODEX_HOME`, then `CODEX_HOME`, then `~/.codex`. Existing TOML settings are preserved, with a private config backup before changes. `--no-motion` disables Codex's native animations. ## Real account allowance: source and scope | Connection | What can be shown accurately | What is not assumed | | --- | --- | --- | | OpenAI / ChatGPT OAuth | Account-reported plan, usage percentages, reset windows and named additional pools | A Plus subscription is not a fixed token package; API keys are not Plus logins | | OpenRouter | API-reported free-model daily request counters and effective/key spending cap, when returned | Credit caps are not token totals or necessarily your account balance | | Groq | Actual inference response headers: requests/day and tokens/minute, scoped to the observed model/account | Public tier tables are not your exact current account allowance | | NVIDIA NIM | Actual remaining quota headers, when the response exposes them | No guessed 40 RPM cap, fixed free tokens or unlimited usage | | OpenCode Console | The host's `experimental.usage.limits` subscription/budget counters, when available | Free-model capacity/reset is not invented when the Console API omits it | | Other providers / Orca Router | Local recorded usage, with quota explicitly unavailable | No unverified service endpoints or fabricated allowance | Groq/NVIDIA counters appear after a real model response supplies headers. Capturing headers does not consume the response body or send a test model request. Switching accounts/models isolates their observations. Old observations are marked stale; failed checks never become a false zero or a fresh unlimited allowance. `opencode-install` uses the active saved OpenCode connection; it does not silently substitute your Codex account. Token-sharing logins can deny the OpenAI usage endpoint; the panel reports that limitation rather than estimating your plan. If OpenCode uses token-sharing and its token cannot read allowance, you can explicitly link an existing **same ChatGPT account** Codex login: ```sh ocquota opencode-install --theme sakura --animation sakura --speed 0.75 --link-codex-account ``` The panel labels this **Shared plan via linked Codex** and explicitly says the OpenCode app-specific cap is not exposed. This does not create a second allowance or prove that the two logins are the same account; enable it only after confirming that yourself. The server part reads `auth.json` on the OpenCode server machine; for remote hosts, your local Codex login is not silently transferred. The server uses fixed HTTPS quota endpoints with timeouts and redirects disabled. Only sanitized counters are cached in memory. No credentials or prompts are logged, written to quota cache files or included in reports. ## Codex right-side companion pane ```sh ocquota pane --theme sakura --animation sakura --speed 0.75 ``` In Windows Terminal this opens a right-hand split. On macOS/Linux inside tmux, it opens a right-hand split with a 42-column panel. Other terminals, including VS Code, can be split vertically with their own UI; run this on the right: ```sh ocquota panel --source codex --theme sakura --animation sakura --speed 0.75 ``` The compact panel reads real allowance from the existing Codex OAuth login and shows local tokens separately. The model label comes from the latest recorded session log; without a Codex UI extension API it cannot observe an unsubmitted model-picker change. With multiple Codex sessions, it follows the latest modified record, not a guaranteed binding to one terminal. The read-only companion does not refresh or replace Codex's credentials. Keychain-only/API-key logins without a usable `auth.json` OAuth token show allowance unavailable. ## Pick a theme The ten new themes join Aurora, Ember and Mono. All thirteen are available for the standalone CLI, OpenCode (light and dark) and Codex syntax/footer themes. | Theme | Palette | Default scene | | --- | --- | --- | | `sakura` | Cherry blossom pink / soft violet | Sakura | | `forest` | Fern green / woodland | Leaves | | `ocean` | Tidal blue / sea glass | Waves | | `midnight` | Indigo / silver | Stars | | `matcha` | Moss / oat | Wind | | `lavender` | Lilac / muted blue | Fireflies | | `rose` | Rose clay / warm blush | Sakura | | `sand` | Linen / soft gold | Wind | | `glacier` | Pale cyan / ice blue | Snow | | `neon` | Lime / lilac | Rain | | `aurora` | Cyan / violet | Stars | | `ember` | Amber / coral | Embers | | `mono` | Neutral ink | Snow | `--theme raw` keeps the original quota-bar layout. Preview any theme without a database with `ocquota preview --theme forest --animation leaves`. ## Ten scenes, at your pace | Scene | Motion | | --- | --- | | `sakura` | Cherry petals drifting down | | `rain` | Light vertical rainfall | | `leaves` | Green leaves drifting with a breeze | | `wind` | Horizontal wisps | | `snow` | Slow snowflakes | | `fireflies` | Gently flickering lights | | `stars` | Quiet twinkling sky | | `bubbles` | Rising rings | | `embers` | Warm rising sparks | | `waves` | A moving wave line | ```sh ocquota watch --theme forest --animation leaves --speed 0.5 ocquota watch --source codex --theme ocean --animation waves ocquota watch --theme mono --no-motion ``` In an interactive watch terminal: **Space** pauses, **n** changes scene, **+ / -** adjusts speed and **q / Ctrl-C** exits. Stats keep refreshing while motion is paused. `--speed` accepts 0.25–3; it changes movement speed without increasing frame rate. The current scene and speed are shown in the strip. `OCQUOTA_ANIMATION` and `OCQUOTA_SPEED` set CLI defaults. Set `OCQUOTA_REDUCED_MOTION=1` to disable ambient motion and meter interpolation. For a persistent OpenCode setup without motion, run: ```sh ocquota opencode-install --theme sakura --no-motion ``` Ambient motion is confined to a small fixed strip, capped at 24 particles and roughly 6 frames/second. Data refreshes independently, using cached/incremental reads. Timers stop on disposal; watch restores the terminal and input mode on exit. Piped watch output is one static report. Glyph appearance depends on your terminal font; modern Windows Terminal, macOS Terminal and iTerm2 work best. The README SVG banner also respects browser reduced-motion preferences. ## Reports and budgets ```sh ocquota # today's local quota ocquota watch --limit 5000000 --window day ocquota watch --source codex --window week ocquota bar --metric cost --limit-cost 20 # OpenCode only ocquota oneline ocquota json ocquota totals ocquota models ocquota daily --days 14 ocquota top --n 10 ocquota explain ``` Every report supports `--source opencode|codex`. Windows, macOS and Linux use native paths; quote paths with spaces: ```powershell ocquota watch --source codex --codex-home "C:\Users\Your Name\.codex" ocquota watch --db "C:\path with spaces\opencode.db" ``` Default OpenCode database: `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`. Default Codex logs: `~/.codex/sessions` and `~/.codex/archived_sessions`, including plain and Zstandard-compressed JSONL. On Windows `~` means your user profile. WSL keeps its own sessions; run ocquota inside WSL to read those sessions. Config lives at `~/.config/ocquota/config.json`. Precedence is CLI → environment → config file → defaults. Useful options: | CLI | Environment | Purpose | | --- | --- | --- | | `--db` | `OCQUOTA_DB` | OpenCode SQLite database | | `--source` | `OCQUOTA_SOURCE` | Usage source | | `--codex-home` | `OCQUOTA_CODEX_HOME`, `CODEX_HOME` | Codex home | | `--theme` | `OCQUOTA_THEME` | Appearance | | `--window` | `OCQUOTA_WINDOW` | `day`, `week`, `month` | | `--limit` | `OCQUOTA_LIMIT` | Local token budget | | `--limit-cost` | `OCQUOTA_LIMIT_COST` | Local cost budget, or `none` | | `--metric` | `OCQUOTA_METRIC` | `tokens` or `cost` | | `--refresh` | `OCQUOTA_REFRESH_MS` | Data refresh interval (250ms minimum) | | `--tz` | `OCQUOTA_TZ` | IANA zone or UTC offset | | `--animation` | `OCQUOTA_ANIMATION` | Decorative scene | | `--speed` | `OCQUOTA_SPEED` | Movement multiplier | Day/week/month windows follow your selected timezone, including DST. Cached reads are excluded from the token budget. Session logs are deduplicated; file changes are incrementally parsed. OpenCode access is read-only and native plugin reads fail quickly on busy databases. No telemetry or external reporting. Account panels make authenticated read-only quota requests to the corresponding provider; local reports remain offline. ## Build and verify ```sh bun install --frozen-lockfile bun run typecheck bun run build bun test bun run build:windows ``` The Windows build writes `dist/windows-x64/ocquota.exe` with native plugin files, licenses and docs. Keep the folder together. CI builds a downloadable ZIP and tests offline npm installation, standalone installation, real OpenTUI rendering, settings preservation, light/dark contrast and Windows/macOS/Linux compatibility. ```sh npm pack npm install -g ./kyzenn.raw-ocquota-0.4.0.tgz ``` The npm package includes the bundled CLI, native server/RPC/TUI parts and licenses. `npm publish` runs type checking and tests first. Publishing requires npm login. The [logo](assets/logo.svg) and [animated banner](assets/banner.svg) are original SVG assets; `docs/preview.html` is a local visual-review page.
